name: Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: PALICC (Pediatric Acute Lung Injury Consensus Conference) Criteria

criteria.description: Acute onset of respiratory symptoms within 7 days of a known clinical insult
Impaired oxygenation defined by oxygenation index (OI) ≥4 or oxygen saturation index (OSI) ≥5
Bilateral infiltrates on chest imaging not fully explained by effusions, lobar/lung collapse, or nodules
Respiratory failure not fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met including acute onset, hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, and exclusion of cardiac failure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: PALICC criteria adapted specifically for pediatric patients to improve diagnostic accuracy

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis
Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, procalcitonin) if infectious etiology
Normal or low brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) to exclude cardiogenic edema
imaging: Chest X-ray showing bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates
Chest CT scan may show ground-glass opacities and consolidation
other: Echocardiography to exclude cardiac causes of pulmonary edema

redFlags: Progressive hypoxemia despite maximal oxygen support
references: Pediatric Acute Lung Injury Consensus Conference Group. Pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome: consensus recommendations from the Pediatric Acute Lung Injury Consensus Conference. Pediatr Crit Care Med. 2015 Jun;16(5):428-39.

Khemani RG, Smith L, Lopez-Fernandez YM, et al. Pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome: definition, incidence, and epidemiology: proceedings from the Pediatric Acute Lung Injury Consensus Conference. Pediatr Crit Care Med. 2015 Jun;16(5 Suppl 1):S23-40.
Flori HR, Glidden DV, Rutherford GW, Matthay MA. Pediatric acute lung injury: prospective evaluation of risk factors associated with mortality. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2005 Sep 1;171(9):995-1001.
